idiom_name: key type with a fileprivate initialiser, used from the same file as the authorised collaborator (file-scoped grant); internal/package for wider grants
implementation_notes: Swift's private restricts use to the enclosing declaration and to extensions of that declaration in the same file, and Swift has no friend-to-type, so a key's initialiser cannot be opened to one chosen type. The narrowest workable grant is therefore fileprivate (the file) or internal/package (the module or package): put the key type and the authorised collaborator in one file and mark the initialiser fileprivate, so only that file can mint keys while any caller holding one can use the restricted operation. Because no entity can be defined in terms of a less accessible type, the operation itself must be at least internal, so the pattern works inside an app or framework rather than across modules.
pitfalls: private on the initialiser would restrict it to the key type itself, so the authorised collaborator could not mint one - choose fileprivate deliberately.
The grant is the file: every type in that file, including helpers added later, can mint keys.
A public operation cannot take a fileprivate parameter type; the restricted operation stays internal or narrower, which caps how far a key can travel.
